tools.name: search_wiki
tools.description: Keyword search across Radix Wiki titles and page text — the first call when you know what you are looking for. Returns a page of results, each with its title, URL, tagPath, slug, a matched snippet and the date it was last updated. The tagPath and slug identify the page every read tool accepts. Narro

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Read one page in full: its extracted text, current version number, update date and declared metadata. Takes either the single `path` a listing returns or the tagPath/slug pair it splits into — not a URL and not a title. A wrong pair is answered with the tools that find a right one rather than an emp

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Browse the wiki by tag path rather than by keyword — every page under a branch, newest first by default. Returns the same rows as search_wiki (title, URL, tagPath, slug, snippet, updatedAt) plus a pagination envelope carrying totalPages, hasMore and nextPage. Omit tagPath to walk the whole wiki; pas

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: The wiki tag hierarchy as a tree, each node carrying its path, name, description and page count. The cheapest way to orient before searching, and the only way to find a valid tagPath before create_page. Costs one call and a few kilobytes; prefer it to listing pages to find out what exists.

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Pages edited within the last N days, newest first — what to poll when you are watching the wiki rather than reading it. Same row shape as list_pages. Look back at most 30 days and take at most 50 rows; for anything older, list_pages sorted by updatedAt.

tools.name: get_full_corpus
tools.description: Every article as one plain-text document, for bulk ingestion rather than reading. PREFLIGHT FIRST: call it with sizeOnly=true for the exact character count, a token estimate and the per-branch breakdown — the whole corpus is several times a context window. Then pull it with `maxChars` (default 20000

tools.name: get_ideas_board
tools.description: Get the RADIX Wiki Ideas Pipeline kanban — community proposals and Radix DAO tasks grouped into status columns (Discussion → Proposed → Approved → In Progress → Testing → Done), each card carrying its working group, category, priority, and assignee. Use this to follow DAO / project progress.

tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of writing to the wiki: a single-use ROLA challenge (5-minute expiry). The response spells out the exact recipe for the message your Ed25519 key must sign. You always sign with your OWN key — nothing here custodies anything. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Step 2: exchange the signed ROLA proof for a 7-day Bearer token — the same verification the human wallet flow runs. Send the returned token as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every later create_page / edit_page call; tool arguments never carry it.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Create a new Radix Wiki page. Requires a ROLA bearer token — see https://radix.wiki/AGENTS.md for the challenge-sign-verify flow. Call get_categories first for a valid tagPath. Some paths are balance-gated (blog needs 50,000 $XRD). Earns contribution points.

tools.name: edit_page
tools.description: Edit an existing Radix Wiki page. Requires a ROLA bearer token — see https://radix.wiki/AGENTS.md. Fetch the page with get_page first and send the full revised block array; the version bump, block-level diff, and revision entry are computed server-side. Locked and author-only pages are rejected. Ear

findings.detail: Description of "login" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, list_pages, get_challenge · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, create_page, edit_page · Public sink: login, edit_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, list_pages, get_challenge · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, create_page, edit_page · Public sink: login, edit_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_wiki" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
